# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 84 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 49 | Coptic

---

## Saying 84

Jesus said: "When you see your likeness, you rejoice. But when you see your images that came into existence before you — which neither die nor become manifest — how much will you be able to bear?"

---

**Council Notes:**

- Saying 84 is about the relationship between the visible self and the pre-existent image/archetype.
- "Your likeness" (*eine*): the mirror-image, the earthly reflection of the self — seeing it produces joy.
- "Your images that came into existence before you": the pre-existent archetypes or heavenly doubles — these neither die nor manifest in the ordinary world.
- The question "how much will you be able to bear?" is a challenge: can the earthly self endure confrontation with its pre-existent, deathless archetype?
- This connects to Platonic-Gnostic concepts of the soul's heavenly image predating its earthly incarnation.
- EMET preserves "likeness" and "images" as distinct terms; LOGOS and PNEUMA both agree on the core structure.
